title: Reproduce exact Moran fixation probabilities
statement: For a well-mixed Moran population of N=20 individuals, with no mutation and constant relative mutant fitness r in {1/2,1,2}, compute the probability that a single mutant reaches fixation before extinction. At each discrete update, choose a reproducing individual proportional to fitness and independently choose a uniformly random individual for replacement, including the reproducer. Use exact arithmetic to solve the absorbing-chain equations and reproduce u_1=(1-r^(-1))/(1-r^(-20)) for r≠1 and u_1=1/20 for r=1.
source_locator: McCandlish et al., equation (1) and Section 2; Adlam and Nowak, Introduction and equation (1).
status_basis: The sources give the known formula and update rule. The population size, fitness values and exact-arithmetic deliverable are curator-selected calibration conditions.
plain_summary: Calculate the chance that one mutant eventually replaces a whole idealized population. Exact finite-state calculations make the assumptions and arithmetic inspectable before more complicated evolutionary models are considered.
assumptions: The population contains exactly 20 individuals and each is mutant or wild type; mutation, migration and spatial structure are absent.
Wild-type fitness is 1 and mutant fitness is the fixed positive number r; fitness is independent of frequency and time.
Parent selection is proportional to fitness; replacement is independent and uniform over the original population, allowing a self-replacement event.
State i is the number of mutants. States 0 and 20 are absorbing; the initial state is i=1.
scope: Three fixed rational fitness values in a discrete-time, well-mixed Moran process. No estimation of biological fitness or extrapolation to other update rules.
target: An exact transition specification, absorbing-probability vector for each parameter value, and a proof that its first interior entry matches the known formula.
success_criteria: State all transition probabilities and show that each row sums to one with nonnegative entries.
Solve u_i=p_i^+u_(i+1)+p_i^0u_i+p_i^-u_(i−1), with u_0=0 and u_20=1, in exact arithmetic for each r.
Check every residual and boundary value exactly, and justify uniqueness by almost-sure absorption in this finite chain.
Compare u_1 with the cited formula; treat r=1 separately or use a justified limit.
Keep empirical biological applicability outside the mathematical certificate.
known_results: The Moran fixation probability is a classical result; McCandlish et al. express it using s=log(r), while Adlam and Nowak use relative fitness r.
The neutral value is the continuous limit 1/N. Formula agreement at a few parameter values is not evidence for the adequacy of a population model.
prerequisites: Finite Markov chains and absorbing-state boundary equations.
Rational arithmetic and basic linear algebra.
The distinction between a stochastic update rule and a diffusion approximation.
significance: A compact benchmark for translating biological assumptions into an exact stochastic model. It can reveal update-rule mistakes and spurious agreement from simulation while making no novel evolutionary claim.

relations.explanation: The log-concavity calibration studies the same known single-mutant formula analytically; the present task checks its finite-chain interpretation.

requirements.experiment: None for the formal calculation. Estimating fitness or checking a real population would require biological evidence and a separate task.
requirements.data: Only the stated N and r values; no sequence, clinical or experimental dataset.
requirements.compute: Three systems with 19 unknown interior probabilities and exact rational coefficients. A local exact-arithmetic environment is a plausible resource class; runtime, memory and cost have not been measured.
requirements.theoretical_assumptions: Fixed population size, constant selection, no mutation and the specified well-mixed birth–death update.

ai_assessment.rationale: Small exact systems, explicit update rules and a published formula provide independent checking routes. Priority concerns a future calibration, not an assessed ability to solve open evolutionary questions.

clarity.reason: All states, parameters, endpoints and update choices are fixed.

decomposability.reason: Transition construction, exact solution and interpretation can be reviewed separately.

methods.reason: The sources supply the stochastic model and exact comparison formula.

search_or_symbolic.reason: Finite rational linear algebra supports exact residual checks.

checkability.reason: Every interior equation and boundary condition has a finite certificate.

expertise.reason: A reviewer must recognize how birth, death and population structure affect the model.

significance.reason: Useful model-translation calibration; it does not improve a biological prediction.

verification_difficulty.reason: Exact residual checking is small; absorption and update conventions still need explanation.

ai_assessment.uncertainty: No AI trial was run. A familiar formula may be reproduced from memory, so success would measure a controlled reproduction and checking task rather than novel discovery.
ai_assessment.model_scope: No named model evaluated; assumes tool-using AI with exact rational arithmetic, elementary probability and human review of the update rule.

obstacles: Confusing r with log(r), or importing a diffusion approximation as an exact finite-population result.
Silently changing which individuals can be replaced.
Using Monte Carlo agreement instead of an exact probability certificate.

steps: Translate the update rule into p_i^+=r i(20−i)/(20(ri+20−i)) and p_i^-=i(20−i)/(20(ri+20−i)); derive the self-loop by subtraction.
Build the three exact finite systems and retain their coefficients and solution vectors.
Check residuals with an independently written evaluator and establish almost-sure absorption.
Match the source variables s=log(r), N=20 and the single-mutant initial condition.
Have a probability or population-genetics reviewer inspect the update rule and the scope of the conclusion.
validation.human_review_difficulty: Low to moderate: arithmetic is finite, but a reviewer must confirm that the stochastic model matches the claimed reproduction.
validation.statement_alignment: An exact solution certifies fixation for this transition matrix only. It does not certify Wright–Fisher dynamics, frequency-dependent selection or structured populations.

known_attempts: McCandlish, Epstein and Plotkin (2015) analyze the established fixation formula and attribute the underlying process to Moran.
Adlam and Nowak (2014) use the well-mixed formula as a reference for structured populations.
unresolved_checks: Select an exact-arithmetic representation and independent checker before a trial.
Confirm that any implementation retains self-replacements; omitting them changes transition timing even when the fixation probability happens to agree.
